chunks: Yunus, from the one who narrated it, said:

The master of the slave is liable for qisas regarding the wound of his slave from the value of his diyah; according to that reckoning, the compensation for the wound is determined. And when a free man wounds a slave, the value of his wound is calculated from the reckoning of his value.

key_terms.أَرْشُ: monetary indemnity assessed for a wound
key_terms.الْحُرُّ: a free person, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the slave who is the subject of the injury ruling
key_terms.دِيَتِهِ: his diyah, the legally assessed blood-compensation
key_terms.قِصَاصُ: retaliatory liability or legal requital for an injury
key_terms.قِيمَتِهِ: his market value used as the basis of calculation
key_terms.مَوْلَى: the master or owner legally responsible in this context

ai.seo_question: How is compensation for wounding a slave calculated in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a fiqh ruling regarding compensation and qisas for wounds involving a slave. It explains that the financial assessment of the injury is tied to the slave’s assessed value and diyah framework.
